ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangle with width 8 and height 5. There is one dashed fold line on each of the left and right sides: the left dashed line connects from the lower-left corner to a certain point on the upper side, and the right dashed line connects from the lower-right corner to a certain point on the upper side. After the two upper corners are folded down, the images of their corner points are represented with dotted lines, and the two dotted lines meet at the same point inside the rectangle. Reasoning: Let the bottom side of the rectangle be AB=8, and the height be AD=BC=5, where A is the lower-left corner, B is the lower-right corner, C is the upper-right corner, and D is the upper-left corner. Let the point of the left fold line on the upper side be P, the point of the right fold line on the upper side be Q, and the two folded-down corner points meet at O. Let DP=x, CQ=y. Folding preserves length unchanged, so after the upper-left corner D is folded to O, there is AO=AD=5, PO=DP=x; after the upper-right corner C is folded to O, there is BO=BC=5, QO=CQ=y. Because AO=BO=5 and AB=8, O is on the perpendicular bisector of AB, and its x-coordinate is 4; its height to AB is sqrt(5^2-4^2)=sqrt(9)=3, so O=(4,3) can be taken. Take A=(0,0), B=(8,0), D=(0,5), C=(8,5), then P=(x,5). From PO=x, obtain (4-x)^2+(5-3)^2=x^2, that is, (4-x)^2+4=x^2, solving gives 16-8x+x^2+4=x^2, so 20=8x, x=5/2. Similarly for the right side, y=5/2. Therefore the upper base PQ=8-x-y=8-5/2-5/2=3. The lower base of the obtained trapezoid is 8, the upper base is 3, the height is 5, and the area is (1/2)(8+3)·5=55/2.

raw_record.question_text: A rectangular piece of paper with side lengths 5 by 8 is folded along the dashed lines shown below, so that the folded flaps just touch at the corners as shown by the dotted lines. Find the area of the resulting trapezoid.\n<image1>

method.method_draft: Label the rectangle A( bottom-left ), B( bottom-right ), C( top-right ), D( top-left ), with AB=8 and AD=5. Let P be the left dashed fold point on the top edge, Q the right dashed fold point, and O the common interior point where the two dotted folded corner images meet. Let x=DP and y=CQ. From the image, folding the left flap sends D to O, so the dotted segments give AO=AD=5 and PO=DP=x; similarly BO=BC=5 and QO=CQ=y. Since AO=BO=5 and AB=8, O lies above the midpoint of AB, so its height is sqrt(5^2-4^2)=3, i.e. O=(4,3). With P=(x,5), impose PO=x: (4-x)^2+(5-3)^2=x^2, giving x=5/2. By the same right-side equation y=5/2. Thus the top base PQ is 8-x-y=3, the bottom base is 8, and the trapezoid height is 5. Area = (1/2)(8+3)5 = 55/2.

method.method_draft: Label A as the bottom-left corner, B as the bottom-right corner, D as the top-left corner, and let P be the left dashed fold point on the top edge. Let O be the common point where the folded corners touch. From the dotted folded edges, AO=AD=5 and BO=BC=5; with AB=8, triangle AOB is isosceles with sides 5,5,8, so the midpoint of AB gives a 3-4-5 triangle and the ray AO has direction with sin alpha=3/5 and cos alpha=4/5, where alpha is the angle AO makes with the bottom edge. The crease AP is the reflection axis taking AD to AO, so AP bisects the angle between the vertical ray AD and the ray AO. Hence the angle theta of AP above the horizontal is theta=(90 degrees+alpha)/2. Using tan theta=(1+sin alpha)/cos alpha=(1+3/5)/(4/5)=2. Since P is on the top edge, AP rises 5 units with horizontal run DP=x, so 5/x=2 and x=5/2. The right side is symmetric or obtained identically, so the top base is 8-2x=3. The resulting trapezoid area is (1/2)(8+3)5=55/2.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a rectangle with width 8 and height 5. There is one dashed fold line on each of the left and right sides: the left dashed line connects from the lower-left corner to a certain point on the upper side, and the right dashed line connects from the lower-right corner to a certain point on the upper side. After the two upper corners are folded down, the images of their corner points are represented with dotted lines, and the two dotted lines meet at the same point inside the rectangle. Reasoning: Let the bottom side of the rectangle be AB=8, and the height be AD=BC=5, where A is the lower-left corner, B is the lower-right corner, C is the upper-right corner, and D is the upper-left corner. Let the point of the left fold line on the upper side be P, the point of the right fold line on the upper side be Q, and the two folded-down corner points meet at O. Let DP=x, CQ=y. Folding preserves length unchanged, so after the upper-left corner D is folded to O, there is AO=AD=5, PO=DP=x; after the upper-right corner C is folded to O, there is BO=BC=5, QO=CQ=y. Because AO=BO=5 and AB=8, O is on the perpendicular bisector of AB, and its x-coordinate is 4; its height to AB is sqrt(5^2-4^2)=sqrt(9)=3, so O=(4,3) can be taken. Take A=(0,0), B=(8,0), D=(0,5), C=(8,5), then P=(x,5). From PO=x, obtain (4-x)^2+(5-3)^2=x^2, that is, (4-x)^2+4=x^2, solving gives 16-8x+x^2+4=x^2, so 20=8x, x=5/2. Similarly for the right side, y=5/2. Therefore the upper base PQ=8-x-y=8-5/2-5/2=3. The lower base of the obtained trapezoid is 8, the upper base is 3, the height is 5, and the area is (1/2)(8+3)·5=55/2.
